content.comment_body: Announcement: Phase-out for [product_name] [version_no]. Effective immediately, [product_name] [version_no] models are now categorized as phase-out. Details include product designations and [article_no]s for various sub-types, all compatible with [product_name] [version_no]. Existing programs and extension modules remain usable without restriction. To program the new sub-types, [product_name] [version_no] is required. A free upgrade can be found at [url]. Please note: The [product_name] upgrade download is subject to export regulations.
Can you clarify what it means when a product is designated as 'phase-out'? Will it lose support?

To clarify, what do you specifically mean by support? With a product phase-out, production by [company_name] continues for a limited time (typically about a year) and sales persist during this period. Once discontinued, the item will only be available as a spare part, often at higher prices. For reference, here is a link to [article_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are concerned about the consequences of the phase-out status for [product_name] hardware. There is uncertainty about future support and product availability. The announcement causes confusion regarding the continued support after phase-out, implications for spare parts and service costs, and software compatibility. The requirement for [product_name] [version_no] software for new sub-types emphasizes the importance of software in transitioning to updated hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear information explaining the effects of phase-out on support, ongoing product availability, and continued compatibility. They hope that use of existing programs and extensions will not be interrupted.
